# Chilled Water Plant Sequence of Operations (Draft)

**Assumptions to confirm (flagged in Section 12):**
- N+1 means the design load is at or below 1,600 tons, with one 800-ton chiller as standby.
- CHW ΔT is 12 °F (800 tons at 1,600 gpm).
- CHWP and CWP are headered, so any pump can serve any chiller.
- Cooling towers are served by a common condenser water header.
- The chillers, pumps, towers, and BAS are on the essential electrical system.

Bracketed values `[ ]` are adjustable setpoints with the initial values shown.

---

## 1. General

1.1 The plant consists of:
- Chillers CH-1/2/3 (800 tons, centrifugal, VFD)
- Primary pumps CHWP-1/2/3 (VFD)
- Condenser pumps CWP-1/2/3
- Cooling towers CT-1/2/3 (VFD fans)
- Bypass valve FCV-701
- Primary loop flow meter FIT-702
- Remote differential pressure transmitter DPT-710

1.2 The plant runs as a variable primary flow system. Each operating chiller gets a dedicated pump, run in parallel at a common speed.

1.3 **Hospital criticality:** The plant shall maintain N+1 capacity whenever possible. A single failure of any chiller, pump, tower cell, sensor, or valve shall not cause loss of cooling to surgery suites. All failure responses in this sequence are automatic and do not need operator action.

1.4 The BAS shall own all plant sequencing. Chiller-integral controls shall handle chiller safeties, capacity control, and compressor protection. The BAS shall never override a chiller safety.

## 2. Plant Enable

2.1 The plant is enabled when any of the following is true:
- Any AHU or terminal cooling request is active.
- OAT is above `[50 °F]` (adjustable).
- The operator commands the plant on.

2.2 The plant is disabled only by operator command or when no cooling requests exist and the OAT lockout is satisfied. It remains enabled at all times during hospital operation unless the operator disables it.

2.3 Availability of each chiller requires all of the following:
- The chiller is in Auto.
- The chiller has no active safety alarm.
- Its CHW and CW isolation valves are not failed.
- At least one CHWP and one CWP are available.
- At least one tower cell is available.

## 3. Lead/Lag and Rotation

3.1 The BAS shall designate the lead chiller, lag chiller, and standby chiller from the available chillers.

3.2 Rotate the lead assignment by accumulated runtime. Rotate every `[7 days]` or at operator command, equalizing runtime. Rotation shall happen only through a make-before-break transition: start the new chiller, prove it loaded, then stop the old one.

3.3 The operator may manually select the lead chiller.

3.4 The associated pump and CWP runtime are rotated using the same method.

## 4. Chiller Start Sequence

On a command to start a chiller:

1. Open the chiller CW isolation valve and the CHW isolation valve.
2. Start a CWP. Prove flow with the chiller flow switch or DP.
3. Enable the tower sequence (Section 9) and verify the condenser water temperature is above the chiller manufacturer's minimum entering temperature.
4. Start a CHWP at minimum speed `[40%]`, then ramp to the pump control signal. Prove CHW flow.
5. When CHW and CW flows are both proven for `[30 sec]`, enable the chiller. The chiller's internal controls start the compressor.
6. Reset the bypass minimum flow setpoint (Section 7) to include the new chiller's 960 gpm **before** the chiller starts, so the new chiller never sees less than minimum flow.

Stopping reverses this: unload the chiller, stop the compressor, wait for the chiller's post-lube and coastdown, then stop the pumps and close the valves after `[5 min]`.

## 5. Chiller Staging

5.1 **Plant load** is calculated as:
Tons = 500 × FIT-702 (gpm) × (CHWRT − CHWST) / 12,000
The result is low-pass filtered. If FIT-702 fails, use the sum of the chillers' reported capacity.

5.2 **Stage up** (start next chiller) when any of these conditions persists:
- Calculated load exceeds `[90%]` of the operating chillers' rated capacity for `[10 min]`.
- CHWST exceeds setpoint by more than `[1.5 °F]` for `[10 min]` while operating chillers are at or above `[95%]` of full load amperage or capacity limit.
- Pumps are at 100% speed, DPT-710 is below setpoint by `[2 psid]`, and flow is at maximum for `[5 min]`.
- Any operating chiller trips, or any operating CHWP or CWP fails without an available substitute. This is an **immediate** start with no time delay.

5.3 **Stage down** (stop the most-run lag chiller) when all of these hold:
- Calculated load is below `[75%]` of the capacity of the chillers that would remain, for `[15 min]`.
- Flow after stage-down remains above the minimum flow of the remaining chillers.
- No stage-up condition is active.
- The stage-down will not leave the plant without an available standby for the load.

5.4 After any stage change, allow `[20 min]` before another stage change, except for failure-triggered starts.

5.5 Load may exceed the capacity of two chillers (1,600 tons). When all three chillers are required, alarm **"N+1 CAPACITY LOST"** at high priority.

5.6 When there is no cooling demand, the standby chiller remains available with its isolation valves in their last position and its pumps off. The BAS shall confirm availability by status and periodic checks.

## 6. Chilled Water Pump Control

6.1 One CHWP runs for each operating chiller. All running CHWPs share the same speed command.

6.2 **Speed control:** a PID loop modulates pump speed to maintain DPT-710 at `[12 psid]`. Minimum speed is `[40%]`, set so each operating chiller meets minimum flow with the bypass valve at or near closed. Maximum speed limits flow to no more than `[100%]` of design (1,600 gpm per operating chiller).

6.3 **Pump failover:** on pump failure or VFD fault, the BAS starts the standby pump immediately. A pump's failure shall not make its chiller unavailable. Alarm on failover.

6.4 **Pump proving:** use pump status and current. If proof fails within `[30 sec]`, declare failure and fail over.

6.5 **DPT-710 failure:** on a signal out of range or loss of communication, hold pump speed at the last good value for `[1 min]`, then switch to a fixed speed that gives at least the minimum flow plus margin, alarm, and rely on FIT-702 for flow limits. Control the speed to the next-best available differential pressure signal. A second remote DP sensor at a different critical AHU (a surgery AHU) should be provided and the control should use the highest-demand signal or the lowest DP-versus-setpoint sensor. See Section 12.

## 7. Bypass Valve FCV-701 (Minimum Flow)

7.1 **Minimum flow setpoint** = 960 gpm × number of operating chillers (plus any starting chiller during its start sequence).

7.2 A PID loop modulates FCV-701 open to hold FIT-702 at the minimum flow setpoint when measured flow is below it. FCV-701 closes when flow is above the setpoint.

7.3 The valve shall be fully closed during normal operation above minimum flow, and the loop shall have an anti-windup limit.

7.4 During a chiller stage-up, the minimum flow setpoint increases when the start command is issued. During stage-down, it decreases after the chiller is stopped and the isolation valve closed.

7.5 **FIT-702 failure:** drive FCV-701 to a fixed position `[30%]` open, set pumps to a minimum speed that provides at least the minimum flow for the operating chillers, and alarm.

7.6 Each chiller's own flow switch or flow measurement provides the final low flow safety. A low flow condition on any chiller opens FCV-701 fully, raises pump speed to maximum, alarms, and lets the chiller trip if flow is not restored.

## 8. Chilled Water Supply Temperature Setpoint and Reset

8.1 The default CHWST setpoint is `[42 °F]`.

8.2 **Reset:** the setpoint may rise to `[46 °F]` based on AHU coil valve positions, using a trim-and-respond or valve-position-request strategy.
- Every `[5 min]`, if fewer than `[2]` coil valves are above `[95%]` open, trim the setpoint up by `[0.5 °F]`.
- If `[2]` or more are above `[95%]`, or any critical AHU valve is above `[90%]`, respond by lowering the setpoint by `[1.0 °F]`.
- Limit the setpoint between 42 °F and 46 °F.

8.3 **Critical-zone protection:** coil valves on surgery suite and other critical-area AHUs are weighted as critical. Any such valve above `[90%]` open, any such AHU with space humidity above its high limit, or any such AHU with a discharge air temperature alarm prevents the setpoint from rising and drives it back toward 42 °F. Surgery suites need dehumidification, so reset is also disabled while outdoor dewpoint is above `[60 °F]` or at operator command.

8.4 Reset is disabled, and the setpoint returned to 42 °F, if the plant is in a failure mode (Section 10), if N+1 is lost, or during the first `[30 min]` after a plant start.

8.5 The chiller internal controls hold leaving water temperature at the BAS-commanded setpoint.

## 9. Condenser Water and Cooling Towers

9.1 **Condenser pumps:** one CWP runs per operating chiller, with a standby CWP available. The failure response matches Section 6.3.

9.2 **Tower isolation:** each operating chiller and each operating tower cell has its isolation valve open. The BAS shall open the associated valves before starting the pump or fan.

9.3 **Tower fan control:** a PID loop modulates the VFD fans in unison to hold condenser water supply temperature at setpoint.

9.4 **Condenser water supply temperature setpoint:** reset it to wet bulb plus `[7 °F]` approach, with a minimum of the chiller manufacturer's minimum entering temperature (`[55 °F]`) and a maximum of `[85 °F]`. Reduce the setpoint further only where plant kW is reduced overall. Engineer to confirm optimization.

9.5 **Tower staging:** enable the tower cells so the number of cells at least equals the number of operating chillers. Enable the next cell when running fans are above `[90%]` speed for `[5 min]`. Disable a cell when running fans are below `[40%]` for `[10 min]`. Prefer running more cells at lower fan speed.

9.6 **Tower failure:** on a fan or cell failure, enable another cell immediately. Alarm.

9.7 **Freeze protection** (if applicable to the climate): basin heater enable below `[40 °F]` OAT, and basin level controls. Engineer to confirm project requirements.

## 10. Failure Modes and Hospital Resilience

10.1 **Chiller trip:** immediately start the standby chiller using Section 4. Keep the standby sequence prepared, with isolation valves and a pre-opened CW and CHW path. Target full flow within `[5 min]`. Alarm high priority.

10.2 **Loss of N+1:** if any chiller, pump, CWP, or tower cell is unavailable such that redundancy is lost, alarm **"N+1 REDUNDANCY LOST"**, disable CHWST reset, and notify the facility operator.

10.3 **Power failure and restoration:** after loss of normal power and generator transfer, the BAS shall restart the plant without operator action using a staggered sequence.
- Restart pumps and towers first.
- Then start chillers one at a time, with a delay of `[2 min]` between chillers to limit generator inrush.
- The lead chiller starts first, then others as load requires.
- The sequence shall obey the chiller manufacturer's restart timers.

10.4 **BAS communication failure:** the pump VFDs, chillers, and valves shall hold their last state or fail to a safe default. The chillers' internal controls shall keep running independently. FCV-701 shall fail to a position that preserves minimum flow, and isolation valves fail as-is.

10.5 **Sensor failure:** all critical analog inputs (CHWST, CHWRT, CWST, DPT-710, FIT-702) shall be monitored for out-of-range and rate-of-change faults. The failure responses are in Sections 5.1, 6.5, and 7.5. Use redundant sensors where the engineer designates them.

10.6 **Low CHW supply temperature:** if CHWST falls below `[38 °F]`, alarm, and the chiller freeze protection takes priority.

10.7 **High CHW supply temperature:** if CHWST exceeds setpoint by `[4 °F]` for `[10 min]` while any chiller is available, start the standby chiller and alarm high priority.

## 11. Alarms (minimum set)

| Alarm | Priority |
|---|---|
| Chiller fault or trip | Critical |
| N+1 redundancy lost | Critical |
| CHW supply temperature high (> SP + 4 °F, 10 min) | Critical |
| CHWP or CWP failure or failover | High |
| Tower fan or cell failure | High |
| Low CHW flow at any chiller | Critical |
| DPT-710 or FIT-702 sensor failure | High |
| Bypass valve FCV-701 open above `[50%]` for `[15 min]` | Medium (indicates a flow or staging problem) |
| Chiller start failed to prove | High |
| Plant running on emergency power | Informational |
| CHWST reset disabled by critical zone | Informational |

## 12. Open Items for the Engineer to Confirm

1. Confirm the design load is at or below 1,600 tons, which is required for true N+1.
2. DPT-710 is a single point of failure for pump control. Recommend adding at least one more remote DP sensor serving a different critical AHU (a surgery AHU), and control from the worst-case signal.
3. Confirm that the CWPs and tower connections are headered. If the CWPs are dedicated, a pump failure makes the matching chiller unavailable.
4. Confirm the chiller manufacturer's minimum flow, minimum entering condenser water temperature, restart timers, and minimum load. Update the setpoints above to match.
5. Confirm the essential electrical system serves all plant equipment and the BAS controllers. Include UPS on the controllers.
6. Confirm the failure positions of FCV-701 and the isolation valves.
7. Confirm the OR humidity and dehumidification requirements against the CHWST reset limit of 46 °F.
8. Confirm whether the climate needs tower freeze protection, and whether a waterside economizer is wanted in the future.

---

If you want, I can follow this with a points list, a version tied to a particular chiller manufacturer's protocol, or functional test procedures for commissioning.
